launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.summary: Joe Riley Waterfront Park is Charleston's eight-acre harborfront park, with the Pineapple Fountain, a second interactive fountain, shaded garden rooms, lawns, a walking path, and a long pier with swings and picnic tables.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.hours: City parks are closed from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. unless the Parks or Recreation director orders otherwise. Fountains, the pier, City Gallery, permitted events, maintenance, and severe weather can change access independently.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.parking: There is no large dedicated visitor lot. Use legal metered street parking or a downtown public garage, then walk to the park; do not navigate expecting curbside parking beside the Pineapple Fountain.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.arrival: Choose Pineapple Fountain, Vendue Wharf, the splash fountain, or City Gallery before leaving. The park is linear, and the closest cross street changes with the destination.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.restrooms: Do not assume a public restroom is open within every part of the park. Plan around nearby staffed facilities and verify City Gallery hours when relying on that building.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.cost: Ordinary park, pier, lawn, path, and fountain access is free. Downtown parking, permitted events, tours, food, and nearby attractions cost separately.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.accessibility: The principal waterfront path, fountain plazas, pier, and lawn edges use paved or firm routes. Crowds, wet fountain paving, pier transitions, and temporary event barriers can affect movement.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas subject to posted city rules. Keep pets out of interactive fountains and respect event, planting, and building restrictions.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.family: The two fountains, pier swings, boats, lawns, and short paved walks make this an easy family stop, but the open harbor edge and slippery fountain surfaces require close supervision.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.transit: Downtown CARTA and DASH service reaches the historic district. Select a stop based on the fountain, pier, or gallery rather than the broad park pin.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.need: The Pineapple Fountain and splash fountain are different destinations. Fountain operation can pause for cleaning, repairs, weather, or events, and an open park does not guarantee active water.
launch-sc-charleston-waterfront-park.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, coastal flooding, wind, and Charleston emergency alerts. The waterfront has limited shelter and can be affected by king tides and tropical weather.

launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.summary: Hampton Park is one of Charleston's largest city parks, known for extensive floral displays, an old rose collection, arboretum trees, a lagoon, fitness route, playground, picnicking, restrooms, and on-site parking.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.hours: City parks are closed from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. unless otherwise ordered. Vehicles are restricted on Mary Murray Drive for Walk, Run or Roll on Tuesday and Thursday 6:00-8:00 p.m. and Saturday 8:00 a.m.-noon; confirm current signs.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.parking: Use the on-site parking reached from Mary Murray Drive. Weddings, festivals, ball games, Citadel activity, and car-free periods can change circulation and reduce available spaces.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.arrival: The lagoon and gazebo form the most recognizable central destination. The rose collection, fitness trail, playground, and ball field sit in different parts of the park, so choose the subsite before navigating.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.restrooms: Hampton Park is one of the city parks with public restrooms. Availability can still follow maintenance, event, or facility conditions rather than every hour the grounds are accessible.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.cost: Ordinary park, garden, playground, and trail use is free. Weddings, reunions, reserved spaces, programs, and permitted events may require reservations and fees.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.accessibility: Paved drives and walks reach major garden, lagoon, gazebo, restroom, and recreation areas. Older surfaces, lawn routes, roots, and temporary event setups vary.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas under posted city rules. Keep pets out of planted beds, playground spaces, organized fields, and permitted-event areas when restricted.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.family: The lagoon, gardens, broad lawns, playground, trees, and short loop options work well for families. Water edges, vehicle periods, heat, and event crowds still need supervision and planning.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.transit: CARTA service reaches the surrounding peninsula. Confirm the nearest stop for Mary Murray Drive and account for the walk around the park perimeter.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.need: Mary Murray Drive changes from vehicle circulation to a car-free exercise loop at scheduled times. That is useful for walking but changes parking and pickup expectations.
launch-sc-charleston-hampton-park.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, standing water, and Charleston alerts. Shade is substantial in places, but lawns, the lagoon edge, and event areas remain exposed.

launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.summary: Melton Peter Demetre Park, commonly called Sunrise Park, is a small James Island harborfront destination with panoramic city views, a 190-foot fishing pier, floating dock, two sandy beaches, picnic pavilion, and short trail.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. An automatic gate opens and closes at those times; emergency, storm, maintenance, or event restrictions can supersede the normal schedule.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.parking: Use the small on-site lot at the end of Wampler Drive. Parking is restricted and fills quickly around sunrise, pleasant weekends, fishing periods, and special gatherings.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.arrival: Navigate to the Wampler Drive gate, then choose the fishing pier, dock, beach, pavilion, or overlook. This is a neighborhood approach with limited turnaround and no overflow lot promised by the city.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.restrooms: The official feature list does not promise public restrooms. Plan as though none are available unless current signs or the operator confirm otherwise.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.cost: Ordinary park, pier, beach, trail, and picnic access is free. Reserved use and permitted gatherings may cost separately.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.accessibility: The parking area and developed pier or pavilion approaches provide the firmest routes. Sand, the floating dock transition, shoreline, and short natural trail are less predictable.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.dogs: Follow posted city leash and shoreline rules. Keep dogs controlled around fishing activity, wildlife, narrow dock approaches, picnics, and other visitors.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.family: Views, boats, shark-tooth searching, picnics, and the short walk can make a memorable family stop. There is no swimming, diving, or jumping from docks or piers, and there is no lifeguard service.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.transit: This residential James Island destination is easiest to reach by car, bicycle, or rideshare. Confirm return transportation because the park closes behind an automatic gate at 8:00 p.m.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.need: The sandy shoreline looks like a swimming beach, but swimming and diving are prohibited. Do not jump from the pier or floating dock, and leave before the automatic gate closes.
launch-sc-charleston-melton-peter-demetr.weather: Check tide, wind, thunderstorms, coastal flooding, heat, and Charleston alerts. The exposed pier and shoreline are poor places to wait out lightning or tropical weather.

launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.summary: Forsyth Park is Savannah's 30-acre historic central park, with its landmark fountain, shaded walks, lawns, playground, splash pad, Fragrant Garden, courts, bandshell, monuments, farmers market, and frequent events.

launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.parking: Use legal street parking around the park and read meters, street-sweeping, residential, loading, and event restrictions carefully. Large events and the Saturday market can make the closest blocks impractical.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.arrival: The fountain anchors the north half, while playground and splash-pad activity is farther south. Select the exact subsite rather than navigating only to the broad park name.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.restrooms: Restroom availability varies by facility and event. Do not assume a restroom beside the fountain is continuously open; identify the nearest staffed or event facility before a long visit.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.cost: Ordinary park, fountain, lawn, path, playground, and splash-pad access is free. Parking, food, markets, permitted events, rentals, and programs may cost.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.accessibility: Broad paved walks connect major areas, and the city is planning additional accessibility improvements. Historic paving, roots, lawns, crowds, wet splash-pad surfaces, and temporary event layouts vary.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas under posted city rules. Keep pets out of splash-pad and playground activity, respect event restrictions, and clean up immediately.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.family: The playground, splash pad, fountain, lawns, shaded paths, market activity, and open space offer several visit styles. Keep children close around streets, crowds, monuments, and wet surfaces.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.transit: Savannah transit and downtown shuttle options serve the historic district. Choose the north fountain or south recreation end before selecting a stop.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.need: Forsyth is an active civic and event space, not one uniform park experience. Construction, festivals, the farmers market, sports, and future splash-pad improvements can change specific areas while the rest remains open.
launch-ga-savannah-forsyth-park.weather: Check Savannah heat index, thunderstorms, tropical weather, air quality, and event notices. Tree shade is strong along many paths, but lawns, courts, and queues remain exposed.

launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.summary: Daffin Park is a large neighborhood recreation park centered on a lake and walking loop, with Grayson Stadium, seasonal pool, playground and splash-pad project, courts, athletic fields, and broad tree-lined space.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.hours: Outdoor grounds, Grayson Stadium, pool, playground project, splash pad, courts, fields, and programs do not share one reliable schedule. Verify the exact facility; posted 2026 lap-swim programming runs seasonally and is not the park's general schedule.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.parking: Parking is distributed around the park and Grayson Stadium. Baseball games, pool programs, construction, and league play can redirect access or fill the closest spaces.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.arrival: Choose the lake loop, stadium, pool, playground and splash-pad area, courts, or athletic fields first. The park is large enough that a generic pin can leave visitors on the wrong side.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with developed recreation facilities, but hours can follow the pool, stadium, playground project, leagues, or programs. Verify before relying on them.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.cost: Ordinary outdoor park, loop, playground, and casual recreation are generally free. Stadium events, pool programs, reservations, concessions, leagues, and permits may cost.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.accessibility: The loop and developed recreation areas provide the firmest routes. Construction, grass fields, older paving, event barriers, and wet areas can vary.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.dogs: Use a leash and follow posted city rules. Keep dogs out of pools, playground and splash-pad activity, stadium events, and organized athletic fields unless specifically allowed.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.family: The loop, lake, playground, planned splash pad, pool, stadium atmosphere, courts, and fields support many family visits, but confirm which seasonal or construction-dependent features are operating.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.transit: Local bus service reaches the Victory Drive corridor. Match the stop to the stadium side, pool, playground, or lake loop rather than assuming one entrance serves all areas.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.need: The new ADA playground, restroom, and splash-pad work has changed this corner of the park. Verify current construction and opening status instead of treating a project announcement as proof every feature is operating.
launch-ga-savannah-daffin-park.weather: Check Savannah heat index, thunderstorms, field conditions, and tropical-weather alerts. The lake, pool, fields, and splash-pad operation can each respond differently to weather.

launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.summary: Lake Mayer is a 75-acre Chatham County community park with a 1.5-mile paved loop, stocked freshwater lake, fishing pier, boat ramp, playground, dog exercise area, courts, hockey rink, ball field, community center, and accessible parking.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.hours: The park is listed as open, but the official page does not publish one complete outdoor gate schedule. The Community Center office is open Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.; programs, rentals, courts, and events vary.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.parking: Use the developed lots serving the community center, playground, courts, stadium, and lake. Choose the destination first because the 75-acre site and adjacent facilities have separate approaches.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.arrival: The paved loop circles the lake, while the playground, dog area, courts, hockey rink, fishing pier, boat ramp, and community center occupy distinct nodes shown on the county map.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.restrooms: The county lists bathrooms at Lake Mayer. Community Center facilities follow office, program, and rental access, so verify availability outside staffed hours.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.cost: Ordinary park, loop, playground, dog area, and casual use are free. Room or pavilion rentals, registered programs, leagues, and special events may charge.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.accessibility: The county lists accessible parking and the paved loop provides a firm route. Fishing-pier transitions, grass recreation areas, crowded events, and individual sports surfaces vary.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.dogs: A designated dog exercise area is available outdoors. Pets are not allowed inside the Community Center except working service animals; keep dogs attended and follow posted leash and gate rules.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.family: The playground, paved loop, lake, fishing, courts, events, and community programming give families several options. Children must be accompanied during Community Center activities and supervised around water and traffic.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.transit: Public transportation is less direct than in downtown Savannah. Confirm the nearest current stop or plan a car, bicycle, or rideshare arrival to the exact facility.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.need: Lake Mayer is entering a site-specific master-planning process. Current amenities remain listed, but future construction and phased changes may affect routes and facilities, so check county notices before repeat visits.
launch-ga-savannah-lake-mayer-community-.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, lake wind, tropical weather, and county alerts. The loop and sports areas are exposed, and lightning can interrupt water-edge and court activity.

launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.summary: Kathryn Abbey Hanna Park combines 1.5 miles of Atlantic beach, The Poles surf break, a 60-acre freshwater lake, more than 20 miles of trails, campground, seasonal splash park, playgrounds, picnic facilities, concessions, rentals, and accessible paddling.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.hours: Open daily 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. during daylight-saving season and 8:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. during standard-time season. Last entry is 30 minutes before closing; 6:00-8:00 a.m. entry requires a prepaid early-bird or annual pass.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.parking: Enter from Wonderwood Drive and pay at the gate, then follow signs to beach access, lake, splash park, campground, trails, or a reserved pavilion. The park is large; choose the destination before entering.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.arrival: Beach, lake, campground, trails, splash park, and plazas are separate visit zones. The Poles surf break and the freshwater lake are not interchangeable water destinations.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.restrooms: Restrooms serve developed beach, campground, lake, and pavilion areas, but individual buildings and concessions can keep shorter schedules than the gate.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.cost: $5 per car with up to six people or $3 per pedestrian or bicyclist from 8:00 a.m. to closing. Camping, cabins, rentals, reservations, early-bird access, and annual passes cost separately; verify current tax and rates.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.accessibility: The city lists accessible amenities and an adaptive kayak launch. Beach sand, natural trails, campsites, lake edges, and surf access still vary substantially by route and conditions.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.dogs: Pets are permitted only in designated areas, must be attended, well behaved, and on a leash eight feet or shorter. Follow signs around beach, water-play, campground, and natural areas.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.family: The seasonal splash park, lake paddling, playground, beach, camping, rentals, picnics, and easier trails offer several family visit styles. Match the activity to swimming ability, heat, surf, lightning, and supervision needs.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.transit: The oceanfront location is most practical by car. If using bicycle or rideshare, account for the entrance fee, long internal distances, equipment, and a reliable return before gate closing.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.need: Swimming is prohibited in the freshwater lake. The splash park normally operates from the first weekend in May through the last weekend in October, 10:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m., but closes temporarily for maintenance or lightning within ten miles and has no lifeguards.
launch-fl-jacksonville-kathryn-abbey-han.weather: Check surf, rip-current risk, heat index, thunderstorms, lightning, wind, wildfire conditions, and Jacksonville alerts. Beach, lake, trails, splash park, and campground can be affected differently.

launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.summary: Metropolitan Park is an 18.25-acre St. Johns River waterfront park beside Jacksonville's stadium district, with a Riverwalk connection, boat dock, nonmotorized launch, playground, picnic facilities, and a history as a major festival site.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.hours: The official park listing does not publish one dependable daily schedule. Stadium-district events, riverfront construction, permitted use, security operations, and maintenance can alter access; verify the current city listing before visiting.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.parking: Use stadium-district parking only where current signs permit it. Event days can close roads, reserve lots, impose fees, and create long walks, so check the stadium and city event calendar before driving.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.arrival: The riverfront, Riverwalk connection, dock, launch, playground, and former pavilion or event areas are separate. Navigate to the exact subsite and confirm that construction has not changed the approach.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.restrooms: Restrooms are listed as an amenity, but availability can follow events, construction, security, or maintenance rather than continuous park access.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.cost: Ordinary park and riverfront access is generally free. Event parking, permitted festivals, concessions, marina activity, and reservations may cost.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.accessibility: Developed riverfront walks and event surfaces provide the firmest routes. Construction barriers, dock transitions, grass, event equipment, and stadium crowds vary.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor areas subject to posted city and event rules. Keep pets away from playground activity, restricted docks, crowds, and temporary event zones.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.family: River views, boats, the playground, picnics, and Riverwalk can work for families when the district is quiet. Stadium events, construction, heat, and the unguarded river edge require advance planning.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.transit: JTA service and downtown connections can be useful during major events, but routes and stops may move with road closures. Match the trip to the stadium district and exact riverfront destination.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.need: This area has undergone repeated redevelopment planning. Historical descriptions of the pavilion or festival configuration may not match today's site, so verify current access and never treat an older photograph as proof a facility remains.
launch-fl-jacksonville-metropolitan-park.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, river wind, flood conditions, tropical-weather alerts, and event notices. The open riverfront offers limited storm shelter.

launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.summary: White Point Garden is Charleston's 5.7-acre waterfront park at the Battery, with shaded paths, a pavilion, harbor views, historic cannons, monuments, memorials, drinking fountains, and scheduled off-leash dog hours.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.hours: City parks are closed from 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. unless otherwise ordered. The non-fenced off-leash area operates dawn-9:00 a.m. and 5:00-11:00 p.m.; events, weather, and maintenance can change access.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.parking: Use legal curb parking around Murray Boulevard and South Battery where posted. Spaces are limited and disappear during ceremonies, weddings, festivals, storms, and major waterfront events; downtown garages require a walk.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.arrival: The park occupies the peninsula tip between Murray Boulevard, East Battery, and South Battery. Choose the pavilion, harbor walk, cannons, a named memorial, or the off-leash period before arriving.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.restrooms: The official park inventory lists drinking fountains but does not promise a continuously open public restroom. Identify a nearby staffed facility before planning a long visit.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.cost: Ordinary park, path, monument, and harbor-view access is free. Parking, tours, permitted ceremonies, and nearby attractions cost separately.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.accessibility: Perimeter sidewalks and primary park paths provide the firmest routes. Historic surfaces, roots, lawn approaches, memorial edges, crowds, and event equipment vary.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.dogs: White Point Garden is a non-fenced off-leash area only dawn-9:00 a.m. and 5:00-11:00 p.m. Dogs must be leashed outside those periods and whenever leaving the designated area; owners must clean up and maintain control.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.family: Cannons, ships, harbor views, shade, and short walks can hold children's attention, but this is a passive historic park without a playground and with busy streets and an open waterfront nearby.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.transit: Downtown CARTA and DASH routes can reduce parking pressure, but the final approach requires walking through the historic district to the peninsula tip.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.need: This is also an active memorial and ceremony landscape. Do not climb monuments or artillery, interrupt services, or assume off-leash dogs will be absent during designated hours.
launch-sc-charleston-white-point-garden.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, tide, coastal flooding, wind, and Charleston alerts. The waterfront and surrounding streets can be affected by king tides and tropical weather.

launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.summary: Bonaventure Cemetery is a 100-plus-acre public historic cemetery on a Wilmington River bluff, known for live-oak avenues, sculpture, architecture, notable graves, layered local history, and a detailed section-and-road map.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.hours: Open to the public daily 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. Registered after-hours activities may be approved between 6:00-8:00 a.m. or 5:00-8:00 p.m.; ordinary visitors should not rely on those extended periods.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.parking: Enter at 330 Bonaventure Road and follow cemetery traffic signs. Parking and driving occur along an active cemetery road network; never block a service, grave, gate, aisle, or maintenance vehicle.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.arrival: Download the official map before entering and identify the section, named lane, and grave or landmark. The grounds exceed 100 acres, so the main entrance pin is not sufficient for finding individual sites.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.restrooms: Ask at the administrative building or visitor information point about current restroom availability. Do not assume facilities are distributed throughout the cemetery.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.cost: Ordinary respectful public visitation is free. Commercial tours, organized groups, special events, after-hours access, and filming can require registration and fees.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.accessibility: Visitors can drive the principal road network, but older lanes, roots, grass, monuments, curbs, and individual grave approaches vary. Confirm the route to a specific section before leaving the vehicle.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.dogs: Treat the grounds as an active cemetery, not a recreation park. Follow posted animal rules and contact the cemetery before bringing a pet; qualified service animals remain governed by applicable law.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.family: Older children interested in history, art, trees, and local stories may find the visit meaningful. Adults should set expectations for quiet, respectful conduct and close supervision around roads, monuments, and private family activity.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.transit: The cemetery is east of central Savannah and is easiest to navigate by car or a registered tour. Confirm current transit and rideshare pickup before relying on a return from the entrance.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.need: Bonaventure remains an active cemetery. Ghost, paranormal, treasure-hunt, scavenger-hunt, loud, athletic, or disruptive activities are prohibited; organized groups of ten or more and tours for hire must register.
launch-ga-savannah-bonaventure-cemetery.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, mosquitoes, tropical weather, and Savannah alerts. Tree canopy helps, but the large grounds require water and a plan to return to the entrance before closing.

launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.summary: Jessie Ball duPont Park is a compact Southbank park built around Treaty Oak, a roughly 250-year-old live oak whose low, twisting limbs and broad canopy form one of Jacksonville's most recognizable natural landmarks.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.hours: The official park listing does not publish a dependable daily schedule. Use daylight hours unless current signs state otherwise, and verify temporary closures related to tree protection, maintenance, events, or planned park enhancements.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.parking: A small amount of car parking is listed, but the Southbank setting and nearby development can make access tight. Read every curb and lot sign and consider walking from a legal Southbank space.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.arrival: Navigate to 1123 Prudential Drive, then follow the park entrance to Treaty Oak. Do not confuse this destination with other Jacksonville oak landmarks or assume every nearby private lot permits park parking.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.restrooms: The official amenity list does not include restrooms. Plan around nearby public or staffed Southbank facilities rather than expecting one beneath the tree.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.cost: Ordinary park, picnic-table, lawn, and Treaty Oak viewing access is free. Nearby parking, food, events, and private attractions cost separately.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.accessibility: Developed entrances and paths provide access toward the tree and picnic area. Roots, low limbs, lawn, construction, and tree-protection barriers can limit the closest approach.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.dogs: Keep dogs leashed and under close control unless current signs explicitly provide otherwise. Protect the tree's root zone and keep pets away from picnics, low branches, and restoration areas.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.family: The enormous low limbs and shaded lawn create a memorable short stop, but this is not a playground. Children must not climb, hang from, carve, or damage the historic tree.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.transit: JTA and Southbank pedestrian connections may avoid limited parking. Confirm the safest current crossing from the Riverwalk or transit stop because construction can alter the final block.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.need: The Treaty Oak name comes from a 1930s newspaper story rather than a documented treaty. The genuine significance is the approximately 250-year-old live oak and the long preservation effort surrounding it.
launch-fl-jacksonville-jessie-ball-dupon.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, tropical-weather alerts, and Southbank construction notices. Never shelter beneath a large tree during lightning or high wind.

launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.summary: Skidaway Island State Park protects 588 acres of maritime forest and salt marsh along Skidaway Narrows, with six miles of trails, boardwalks, wildlife viewing, interpretive programs, playgrounds, picnic shelters, cabins, yurts, and a large live-oak campground.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.hours: Park grounds and buildings may keep different schedules; confirm the current gate and visitor-center hours before leaving. The Avian Trail and observation tower are currently closed because of bridge damage, and a partial campground renovation is scheduled through early 2027.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.parking: Turn left at the first traffic light after reaching Skidaway Island; some GPS devices miss this turn. A Georgia ParkPass parking fee is required, with separate parking serving the visitor center, trails, shelters, and camping areas.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.arrival: Choose the Jane Hurt Yarn Interpretive Center, Sandpiper Trail, Big Ferry Trail, campground, playground, or shelter before entering. Use the official map because camping loops and trailheads branch from different park roads.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.restrooms: The official map identifies public restrooms, showers, laundry, and visitor facilities at developed nodes. Natural trail segments do not provide continuous facilities.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.cost: A Georgia ParkPass parking fee is required. Camping, cabins, yurts, shelters, bicycle rentals, reservations, and some ranger programs cost separately; verify current rates when booking.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.accessibility: The park provides an accessibility guide, developed visitor facilities, accessible restroom locations, and mapped firm routes. Boardwalk damage, natural roots, mud, marsh edges, and closed bridges can change individual trail suitability.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on park grounds and in campsites. Pets are not allowed in camper cabins, and owners must follow trail, wildlife, campground, and facility restrictions.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.family: Two playgrounds, the interpretive center, short Sandpiper loop, wildlife, boardwalks, Junior Ranger-style programs, camping, and picnic shelters support family visits. Match distance and heat exposure to the youngest visitor.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.transit: The park is about 15 miles southeast of central Savannah and is most practical by car. Rideshare visitors need a dependable return because destinations are spread within the gated park.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.need: Do not plan around the Avian Trail or observation tower until Georgia State Parks removes the current closure notice. Campground construction may also change loop access, noise, and available sites through early 2027.
launch-ga-savannah-skidaway-island-state.weather: Check heat index, thunderstorms, mosquitoes, tide, tropical weather, and Georgia State Parks alerts. Salt marsh, boardwalks, and exposed observation areas offer limited lightning shelter.
